cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Create an Agent Skill that teaches our coding assistant the team's PostgreSQL migration conventions.
expected_outcomes: Classifies the operator context, purpose, invocation mode, and execution type before drafting
Treats team conventions as a preference skill
Names the preference owner or source of truth
Includes an evaluation plan

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring This SKILL.md description just says 'Helps with frontend work.' Rewrite it so the agent knows when to load it.
expected_outcomes: Uses concrete task verbs, artifacts, or tools
Adds plausible negative boundaries
Keeps the description concise

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Review this agent skill and remove instructions that don't change model behavior, like 'write high-quality code.'
expected_outcomes: Identifies no-op guidance
Preserves domain-specific behavioral constraints
Recommends regression checks for substantive changes

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Give me an eval suite for our Terraform skill, including prompts where it must not trigger.
expected_outcomes: Includes positive and neighboring negative routing cases
Separates routing from outcome evaluation
Includes repeated isolated and ablation runs

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Our React skill loads for every Angular ticket. How should I tighten it without missing short React requests?
expected_outcomes: Treats the description as routing logic
Proposes both false-positive and false-negative cases
Avoids solving the issue only with a long exception list

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring A newer model seems to know this API now. Can we delete the skill?
expected_outcomes: Requires enabled versus disabled ablation
Checks repeated trials across relevant harnesses
Keeps evals after retirement

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring My cloud deployment SKILL.md is 760 lines and mixes AWS, Azure, and GCP instructions. Help restructure it.
expected_outcomes: Keeps the common contract, constraints, and resource map in SKILL.md
Moves provider-specific branches into directly and conditionally linked references
Avoids hiding universal safety constraints or duplicating instructions across layers
Keeps resource discovery one hop from SKILL.md

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring I wrote a skill with twelve exact release steps that never vary. Is a skill the right artifact?
expected_outcomes: Recommends a script for deterministic mechanics
Keeps only judgment, constraints, or invocation guidance in a skill if needed

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Can you make our agent's skill stop firing on unrelated requests?
expected_outcomes: Investigates description triggers and negative cases
Requests or inspects representative false-positive prompts

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Design a durable skill for our internal code review conventions and explain how its eval differs from a temporary API-knowledge skill.
expected_outcomes: Classifies internal conventions as a durable preference
Classifies missing API knowledge as a temporary capability
Evaluates preference compliance and capability ablation separately
Defines different maintenance and retirement criteria

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Propose the directory structure for a skill that has shared deployment policy, provider-specific guidance, a deterministic validator, and a manifest template.
expected_outcomes: Places the shared contract and resource map in SKILL.md
Places provider guidance in references
Places deterministic validation in scripts and the static template in assets
Does not create unused placeholder directories

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Review this SKILL.md: it ends with 'see the references folder for more information' and its security rule exists only in references/common.md.
expected_outcomes: Requires direct conditional links that explain when each reference applies
Moves the universally required security constraint into SKILL.md
Avoids deep or generic resource discovery

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Should AWS and GCP be references in one deployment skill or separate skills? Give me a decision rule.
expected_outcomes: Keeps branches as references when they support one shared outcome and contract
Splits skills when branches have independent triggers, contracts, or behavior
Considers loading cost and divergence rather than file size alone

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring What belongs in SKILL.md versus references, scripts, assets, and evals?
expected_outcomes: Defines SKILL.md as the compact contract, decisions, constraints, resource map, and validation guidance
Distinguishes selective knowledge, deterministic mechanics, static inputs, and behavior cases
Keeps critical universal guidance out of optional resources

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Compare how I should design a refund skill for a customer-facing agent versus a pull-request skill for a coding agent I operate.
expected_outcomes: Classifies the refund case as an agent we build whose customer does not know the skill catalog
Prioritizes model routing and realistic shallow prompts for the refund skill
Recognizes explicit user invocation as practical for the operator-facing pull-request workflow
Does not confuse operator context with capability versus preference

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Our skill teaches a brand-new vendor API and our company's naming rules. Is that capability or preference guidance, and should it stay together?
expected_outcomes: Classifies new API knowledge as capability guidance and naming rules as preference guidance
Requires separate eval criteria and retirement lifecycles
Splits them when owners, triggers, or lifecycles diverge
Prevents capability retirement from deleting durable policy accidentally

cases.prompt: /skill-authoring Classify a named documentation-staging workflow that engineers deliberately run and that mostly calls one deterministic command.
expected_outcomes: Classifies it in the agents-we-use context
Prefers user-invoked-only selection for the deliberate workflow
Moves invariant mechanics into a script
Keeps only judgment, inputs, constraints, and result interpretation in a skill if those are needed
